message:
Overnight inactivity report — read-only, no workers launched or recovered.

Evidence:
- Your 03:51 UTC snapshot showed 0/23 Jarvis Workers Working; Workers 4, 6, 7 and 21 were Ready, and the other 19 were Parked.
- Manager's canonical task records the last independently verified Worker launch as Worker 11 at 2026-11-19 22:12:39 UTC. No later qualifying Worker launch is evidenced in the records reviewed.
- Current read-only observations at 14:00 UTC show 0/23 Working and all executions Stopped: eight Ready (Workers 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 19, 21) and fifteen Parked (2, 8-18, 20, 22, 23). Workers 1, 3, 5 and 19 have since received new queued assignments; they are not running sessions.
- The Parked states have concrete dispositions: Workers 8, 14 and 20 have no approved work; Worker 2 is blocked on H1b prerequisites; Workers 9, 12 and 13 await authenticated source/restore prerequisites; Worker 10 completed its earlier a83549a diagnostic; Worker 11 awaits an independent review; Workers 15 and 17 are held on prior Work source/review gates; Workers 16 and 23 are held on C0 authenticated publisher/object visibility; Workers 18 and 22 await the separate Integrator/release and constructor gates.

Cause:
- config/manager/Jarvis.json has the Manager heartbeat disabled and there is no active Jarvis Manager heartbeat schedule. Manager is a browser-session-driven orchestrator, not an always-on daemon; no recurring trigger wakes it while you are away.
- Manager was Ready/Stopped and its state reason explicitly said to observe Lead first and wait for Lead's reconciled Scheduler/Challenges GO/HOLD frontier before dispatching. Lead's standing assignment was Ready/stale and was resumed only when this inbox was invoked at 13:56 UTC. The missing fresh Lead frontier was therefore an intentional dispatch gate.
- Capacity is not established as the cause. Manager has a 10-session budget but no all-account occupancy API; it must use observable Jarvis/Favn Working agents and in-flight launches. The per-agent slotAvailable field is assignment-slot state, not global capacity evidence.
- No evidence shows Worker sessions continuing unobserved: both the 03:51 and current canonical states show zero Working, with current executions Stopped. This is not conclusive proof that no detached backend/browser session existed: no global session inventory is exposed, the connection-diagnostics read failed with TelemetryQuotaExceeded, and local last-seen values are noncanonical.

Next actions:
- Lead has refreshed its canonical task snapshot (task version 112) and is yielding Ready.
- Manager should inspect that snapshot, then dispatch eligible work in order: Worker 6 P0 full .NET 11 Release witness (independent of C0); Worker 5 P1 deterministic planner; Worker 1 P1 Challenge audit; Worker 19 P1 read-only browser smoke; Worker 3 P2 docs reconciliation. Manager alone launches and verifies each session. No reviewer is currently eligible: the shared queue has zero Unclaimed requests.
- C0 blocks only its original-Git publisher/object-visibility work; it does not block the above tasks. Workers 18/22 and other Work tasks remain held by their specific integration/source prerequisites.
- No Operator decision is needed for the current default-off/read-only frontier. Live scheduler activation, canaries or schedule changes, deployment/restart, migration/cutover, and publisher/credential/protected-ref/STOP changes remain explicit-approval gates.
